hypothesis: Exact XML, template, citation, or schema microblocks have sparse deterministic residuals around decoder-available prototypes, allowing a bounded energy-ordered parity decoder to approach direct residual rank and beat causal coding after syndrome, framing, and fallback costs without attempting free-prose search.
interfaces_exposed: deterministic prototype plus sparse residual plus canonical first-hit parity certificate
kill_condition: Retire general Route D if ideal syndrome materially exceeds direct rank, bounded search requires materially more parity than ideal, expansions grow exponentially from 64 through 256 bits, or the constructive payload fails to beat the causal control. Retain only a named structural class if prose fails.
promotion_condition: On frozen development and page-disjoint holdout, exact direct rank and bounded parity search both beat the same causal microblock control after all syndrome, mode, length, matrix, finalization, and source costs; candidate expansions remain within the fixed budget; offset transfer is positive before larger blocks.
rejection_reason: The exact timestamp-envelope Q0 triggered the proposal kill conditions at 1M: selected parity lost 1804 gross bits to the matched causal control, paid economics were -9359.602 B/M, development and holdout bounded success were 0.816 and 0.8387, parity cost was 1.673 times direct-rank delta cost, and 128/256-bit rank expansions were explosive. All logical roundtrips passed, so this is a scientific negative, not infrastructure failure. Reopen only as a new proposal with a materially different decoder-visible structural class and prototype.
retired_neighborhoods: general MOIRAI WRT inference and unrestricted whole-page energy search
title: Seal-2 Route D structural prototype residual microblocks
